clue.text: A serving icon playing — fourth ace in set?

definitions.text: A serving icon playing — fourth ace in set?

indicators.note: playing suggests these letters being put into play and moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
IV is the Roman numeral for four, read here as fourth
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A tennis star with a famous serve fires down yet another ace in a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' shuffles A SERVING ICON together with IV and A. The whole clue doubles as the description: the Croatian Wimbledon champion was famed for serving aces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Croatian player was celebrated for his huge serve and record numbers of aces in a match.

clue.text: Film man and leading couples in scene originally seeing set

indicators.note: leading couples means the front pair of letters from each of the following words

explanation.surface: A director and the main pairs of actors in a scene originally being shown a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first two letters of each word: SC, OR, SE, SE. 'originally' looks like an indicator but is one of the words picked from.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is an American film director, so a man of the movies.

clue.text: Do wrong to take drug on start of this?

definitions.text: Do wrong to take drug on start of this?

indicators.note: to take means the word do holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: X is the cross mark a teacher puts by a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A warning: misbehave by using drugs and you'll be starting on this.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue E 'on' T puts E above T, giving ET, which goes inside DO; X for wrong follows. The whole clue describes what drug-takers end up needing.
explanation.definitionFit: A detox is the cleansing course a drug user undergoes after taking substances.

clue.text: Urgent, filth is back on hospital department

indicators.note: back tells us the letters for filth and is are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: filth means dirt
S is a short form of is, as in it's
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: An insistent complaint that filth is back in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the reversed piece above, so first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident call is loud and insistent, pressing in the way an urgent demand is.

clue.text: Disney film with king ultimately replacing leader over a nation

indicators.note: replacing leader means the opening letter of the film's title is swapped out for another

parts.note: Bambi is the Disney film about a young deer

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Disney film is retitled with a king's name, for a nation's audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'king', G, replaces the B at the front of BAMBI, and A goes after it ('over' in a down clue).
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African country, a nation on the Gambia River.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly dead at the bottom: saw bizarre _________ in reduced Aldi ripening bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: reduced means the shop's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Aldi is a supermarket chain
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone finds a dead spider at the bottom of a box of cut-price ripening bananas in Aldi.
explanation.walkthrough: SAW, BIZARRE, IN, ALD (Aldi reduced), RIPENING and D are rearranged together, with 'bananas' as the anagram signal. The blank in the surface is the first word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous South American spider is a classic creepy-crawly, notorious for turning up in shipments of fruit.

clue.text: Spike prankster's drink

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little prankster
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Somebody spikes the joker's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale something is to pierce it on a spike, so the verb spike fits.

clue.text: See 6
Working score to capture hearts — skill around this?

definitions.text: Working score to capture hearts — skill around this?

indicators.note: working means the letters are being worked into a different order

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: around tells us the word for skill is turned the other way round

parts.note: skill means art

explanation.surface: Players work through a score to win hearts, their skill wrapped around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to capture' just says H joins the shuffled letters; where it lands is free. The whole clue describes the musicians who play a score with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of musicians that plays from a score with skill.

clue.text: Dance and drink: pub closing early

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: closing early means the word for pub loses its last letter, as if shut before time

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: An evening of dancing and drinking, cut short when the pub shuts early.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Unusually par the first: golf club detailed round without experience

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of par appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the first

indicators.note: round means the shortened club is turned around
detailed means de-tailed, the club losing its last letter

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer unusually makes par on the first hole, with a club sent round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed: the club loses its tail before 'round' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from theory or deduction rather than from observed experience.

clue.text: Toy Story character with a way one can fly

parts.note: Buzz Lightyear is the spaceman toy in the Toy Story films
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: Buzz Lightyear insists he has a way to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Buzz famously cannot really fly, which is the joke behind 'one can fly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzard is a bird of prey, something that genuinely flies.

clue.text: Couple from website match.com

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A pair who met through a dating website.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a relationship are called an item, a couple in casual speech.

clue.text: Cycling gear's allure: ride when excited

indicators.note: when excited means these letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: The thrill of a bike ride that gets cyclists excited.
explanation.definitionFit: A derailleur is the mechanism on a bicycle that shifts the chain between sprockets to change gear.

clue.text: One carrying writer on board — one working on plane?

indicators.note: on board means the writing tool is taken inside, like a passenger aboard

parts.note: a carter carries goods by cart
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: An airline worker carrying a writer on board, working on the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the woodworking tool, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter works wood with tools such as the plane, used to smooth timber.

clue.text: Stopped unknown American that's gutted — beat badly boxing

indicators.note: boxing means the shuffled letters enclose the next pieces like a box
badly means the letters of beat are put in a poor, jumbled order

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: gutted means the word loses its insides, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A boxing match was stopped after an unknown American was gutted and beaten badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes ABET from its fodder; 'boxing' puts that around the other pieces. 'Stopped' is the definition, not a boxing term here.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyant describes something held in abeyance, suspended or temporarily halted.

clue.text: Comic hero is about ordinary one rowing

indicators.note: is about means the hero's name goes around the next letter

parts.note: Batman is the comic-book superhero
O is short for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero is in a boat, out rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman is someone who works boats, rowing passengers across water.

clue.text: Player in bar with supporter

parts.note: to bar is to ban
a joist is a beam supporting a floor

explanation.surface: A musician in a bar with a fan backing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjoist plays the banjo, a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Service expert welcoming Queen's total defeat

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: welcoming means the word for expert takes the next letter in

parts.note: an ace is an expert
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A church service with an expert welcoming the monarch ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a massacre is a one-sided rout, a crushing loss.

clue.text: Unchanged by Times? Papers tempt one, surprisingly?

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: surprisingly means the following letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a newspaper that tempts a reader with surprising offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means multiplication: an idempotent element stays the same when multiplied by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics an idempotent quantity is unaltered when multiplied by itself.

clue.text: Model after topless sex show

indicators.note: after tells us the word for model comes behind the shortened word, later in the answer
topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down clue

parts.note: to model is to pose

explanation.surface: A model stars in a topless sex show.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to reveal it, to show what was hidden.

clue.text: Tip: go over with it

indicators.note: over means the word for go sits over and around the word for tip

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt
the end is the tip of something

explanation.surface: Advice: go over it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests advice, but it means END.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is an idiom for fashionable or up to date, just as trendy means.

clue.text: Goddess lives on island

parts.note: lives means is, exists

explanation.surface: A goddess lives on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Important part of bible for homophobe?

parts.note: important means big
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone who uses a key passage of the Bible to justify hating gay people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is an example: a homophobe is one kind of bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: A homophobe is one example of a person intolerant of others, a prejudiced individual.

clue.text: Get rid of old joke, perhaps, for a comeback?

parts.note: ex means former, old
a pun is a joke

indicators.note: for a comeback means the abbreviation goes back the other way

parts.note: EG, for example, means perhaps

explanation.surface: A comedian drops an old gag, maybe to try it again for a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge is to erase or wipe out completely.

clue.text: Men with single publication recalled one model in paper

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men
I is the Roman numeral one, single

indicators.note: recalled means the word for publication is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Men with a single magazine call one model back for a paper shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding, producing figures folded from a sheet.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a problem or point of dispute
... means offspring, as in died without ...

explanation.surface: A worry about the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means both a matter of concern and, in legal language, a person's descendants.

clue.text: Chat in party, taking number from nurse

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: taking, with from, means one letter is taken away from the next word
from completes taking from, the removal of a letter

explanation.surface: A conversation at a party where a nurse takes someone's number.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is talk or conversation, from casual chat to formal discussion.
